papers.title: WildHandBench: A Benchmark for Handwritten Text Understanding that Challenges MLLMs and Humans
papers.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2608.22959
papers.abstract: WildHandBench evaluates 18 state-of-the-art Multimodal Large Language Models across 500 degraded handwritten documents spanning free text, tables, and formulas under nine real-world capture scenarios, introducing the Prior-Driven Error (PDE) metric.

papers.title: Real5-OmniDocBench: A Full-Scale Physical Reconstruction Benchmark for Robust Document Parsing in the Wild
papers.venue: European Conference on Computer Vision (ECCV)
papers.abstract: Real5-OmniDocBench physically reconstructs 1,355 pages of OmniDocBench v1.5 across 6,775 real camera captures under five controlled physical degradation regimes: scanning, uneven illumination and shadows, page warping and folds, screen photography, and 3D perspective skew.

papers.title: Qwen2.5-VL Technical Report
papers.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2502.13923
papers.abstract: Qwen2.5-VL introduces native dynamic-resolution visual processing via window-attention Vision Transformers, absolute coordinate spatial grounding, and structured document and table parsing across 3B, 7B, and 72B open-weight models.

papers.title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS)
papers.abstract: QLoRA introduces 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4), an information-theoretically optimal quantization data type for normally distributed weights, enabling large language and multimodal models to execute on consumer GPUs with minimal accuracy degradation.

papers.title: Patch n' Pack: NaViT, a Vision Transformer for any Aspect Ratio and Resolution
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS)
papers.abstract: NaViT processes arbitrary resolutions and aspect ratios natively via sequence packing rather than distorting images to fixed square grids, substantially improving fine-grained OCR and document layout understanding.

papers.title: OmniDocBench: Benchmarking Diverse PDF Document Parsing with Comprehensive Annotations
papers.venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
papers.abstract: OmniDocBench provides a multi-source benchmark across 1,651 pages and 10 document types, revealing sharp edit-distance degradation when moving from printed pages to handwritten notes.

papers.title: OCRBench v2: An Improved Benchmark for Evaluating Large Multimodal Models on Visual Text Localization and Reasoning
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS)
papers.abstract: OCRBench v2 benchmarks large multimodal models across fine-grained text recognition, text referring, relation extraction, and handwritten mathematical and tabular reasoning.

papers.title: Election Tally Sheets Processing System
papers.venue: 12th IAPR Workshop on Document Analysis Systems (DAS), IEEE
papers.abstract: Evaluates handwritten digit recognition across 64,596 digits written by over 1,000 polling station officials on real electoral tally sheets, demonstrating that models achieving 99.00% on MNIST drop to 66.55% on unadapted tally boxes and 89.32% after Variational Autoencoder and BiLSTM retraining due to bounding-box scale variance.

papers.title: TrOCR: Transformer-based Optical Character Recognition with Pre-trained Models
papers.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
papers.abstract: TrOCR combines a pre-trained Vision Transformer encoder with an autoregressive text decoder for cropped single-line handwritten and printed optical character recognition.

papers.title: olmOCR: Unlocking Trillions of Tokens in PDFs with Vision Language Models
papers.venue: Allen Institute for AI (Ai2) Technical Report, arXiv:2502.18443
papers.abstract: Introduces olmOCR and olmOCR-Bench, demonstrating how fine-tuned 7B vision-language models compare against proprietary frontier APIs across clean PDFs, structured tables, and degraded historical scans.

papers.title: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models on Optical Character Recognition in Dynamic Video and Multi-Domain Environments
papers.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2502.06445
papers.abstract: Evaluates Character Error Rate (CER) and Word Error Rate (WER) across GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Claude 3 Sonnet, EasyOCR, and RapidOCR on noisy multi-domain documents.

papers.title: Digitising HIV Testing Registers to Support National Scale-Up of Three-Test HIV Diagnostic Algorithm: A Case Study of an AI-Powered Monitoring and Evaluation System in Malawi
papers.abstract: Evaluates QED.ai ScanForm across 3,082,406 handwritten clinical records in 545 facilities in Malawi, achieving >99% transcription accuracy through pre-banded templates, local handwriting calibration, and confidence-routed human verification.

papers.title: Using AI to Verify Kenya Election Results: YOLOv5 and AWS Textract on Form 34A
papers.venue: Bob.Africa Engineering Case Study (kenyaelection.live)
papers.abstract: Documents the deployment of a custom YOLOv5 region-of-interest detector (0.9 IoU) paired with AWS Textract across 46,229 Kenyan Form 34A polling station sheets, achieving 97% digit accuracy on cropped quadrants while exposing catastrophic billion-vote row-concatenation failures in the 3% error tail.

papers.title: INEC's Broken Promises: Altered Voting Tallies and Poor Electoral Oversight Cast Doubt Over Nigeria's Presidential Elections
papers.venue: Veza News Forensic Election Investigation Report
papers.abstract: Investigative audit of 2023 Nigerian IReV portal uploads documenting that approximately 77% (2,300 sheets) of Form EC8A uploads in Gombe State were blurred due to dim ambient lighting and detailing manual biro ink alterations on Form EC8A in Rivers State.

papers.title: AI and Civic Tech Are Changing Nigeria's Election Result Tracking Landscape: Mundx Dual-Model Consensus on IReV
papers.venue: Premium Times Nigeria Civic Technology Report
papers.abstract: Describes the Mundx Analytics dual-model Vision AI consensus architecture deployed on Ekiti and Osun State governorship elections, covering 97.7% of IReV polling unit uploads by requiring two independent vision models to agree before accepting a tally.

papers.title: IReV-Sentinel Pro 2.0: Zero-Trust Form EC8A Forensic Audit Engine
papers.venue: AI4Election Hackathon Technical Documentation
papers.abstract: Demonstrates a forensic Form EC8A audit system combining Google Gemini 2.5 Flash optical extraction with deterministic assertions for Electoral Act 2022 Sections 51(2) and 64(4).

papers.title: Electoral Act, 2022 (Act No. 13 of 2022), Sections 51(2), 60(4), and 64(4)
papers.venue: Official Gazette of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
papers.abstract: Establishes the statutory framework governing biometric voter accreditation (BVAS), mandatory polling unit result recording on Form EC8A, over-voting cancellation thresholds under Section 51(2), and collation reconciliation under Section 64(4).

papers.title: Best OCR Tools for Handwriting Recognition: Benchmark on IAM and Multi-Field Medical Registry Forms
papers.venue: Koncile AI Document Intelligence Benchmark Report
papers.abstract: Benchmarks 17 OCR and Vision-Language Models on IAM handwriting lines and 49 multi-field handwritten medical registry forms, finding that while zero-shot VLMs reach 1.75%-2.30% CER on isolated lines, field-level accuracy on full forms plateaus at 85% with a 6% hallucination rate.

papers.title: Shadow Removal and Contrast Enhancement for Mobile-Captured Document Digitization
papers.venue: Proceedings of the International Conference on Islamic Education (ICIE)
papers.abstract: Quantifies smartphone document OCR degradation under cast shadows and low ambient illumination, showing that compound distortions spike Character Error Rate from 14.23% to 22.71%, while shadow removal plus CLAHE reduces CER to 10.84%.

papers.title: Gradient-Based Learning Applied to Document Recognition
papers.venue: Proceedings of the IEEE
papers.abstract: Introduces convolutional neural networks (LeNet-5) and the MNIST isolated handwritten digit benchmark, establishing >99% recognition accuracy on centered, normalized 28x28 grayscale digits.
